description: Deep trace of protium formation showing origin of each coefficient
full_trace:
================================================================================
PROTIUM ℵ(1, 0) = B₃(u_r, u_g, d_b) ⋈ e⁻
DEEP TRACE: where does each coefficient come from?
================================================================================

q = 1.1099785956
q − q⁻¹ = 0.2090603220
s = q^½ − q^(−½) = 0.1043880698

Strands:
  0: u_r (up quark, red)
  1: u_g (up quark, green)
  2: d_b (down quark, blue)
  3: e⁻  (electron)

─── Crossing (0,1): u_r–u_g = u–u ───
  Type: same-flavor quarks → positive crossing
  Element: σ₀  (c = 1, d = 0)

  Before: (+1.0000000000) · 𝟏
  After:  (+1.0000000000) · σ_0
  Reduction: none (σ₀ is already in NF)
  ALL COEFFICIENTS POSITIVE ✓

─── Crossing (0,2): u_r–d_b = u–d ───
  Type: different-flavor quarks → mixed crossing
  Element: (1.000000) · σ₀ + (-0.104530) · 𝟏

  Before: (+1.0000000000) · σ_0
  Product (before reduction):
    (-0.1045301610) · σ_0
    (+1.0000000000) · σ_0 · σ_0

  The product contains σ₀ · σ₀ = σ₀² (Hecke-reducible!)
  σ₀² coefficient: 1.0 × 1.000000 = 1.000000

  *** HECKE REDUCTION (R1) ***
  σ₀² → (0.209060) · σ₀ + 𝟏
  The σ₀² term (1.000000) · σ₀² becomes:
    (1.000000) × (0.209060) · σ₀ = (0.209060) · σ₀
    (1.000000) × 𝟏 = (1.000000) · 𝟏

  After reduction: (+1.0000000000) · 𝟏
    (+0.1045301610) · σ_0

  ★ The 𝟏 coefficient = 1.0000000000
    This came from: Hecke reduction of σ₀²
    The u_r–d_b mixed crossing multiplied against the u_r–u_g
    crossing, producing σ₀². The Hecke relation splits σ₀²
    into (0.209060)·σ₀ + 𝟏. The +1.000000 contribution to 𝟏
    plus the existing (-0.104530) from the d coefficient gives
    the final 𝟏 coefficient: 1.0000000000
    SIGN: POSITIVE → this is binding energy RELEASED

─── Crossing (1,2): u_g–d_b = u–d ───
  Type: different-flavor quarks → mixed crossing
  Element: (1.000000) · σ₁ + (-0.104530) · 𝟏

  Before: (+1.0000000000) · 𝟏
    (+0.1045301610) · σ_0
  Product (before reduction): 4 terms
    (-0.1045301610) · 𝟏
    (-0.0109265546) · σ_0
    (+1.0000000000) · σ_1
    (+0.1045301610) · σ_0 · σ_1

  σ₀ and σ₁ are ADJACENT generators → no σ² but check for far-comm
  After reduction: (-0.1045301610) · 𝟏
    (-0.0109265546) · σ_0
    (+1.0000000000) · σ_1
    (+0.1045301610) · σ_0 · σ_1

─── NEGATIVE COEFFICIENT ANALYSIS (proton B₃ complete) ───
  ★ (-0.1045301610) · 𝟏  ← NEGATIVE (INPUT)
    Origin: d_ud = −½q·s = -0.104530
    The identity coefficient in the u–d mixed crossing
    is NEGATIVE because d = −½q·s < 0.
    This is the Skein amplitude cost of mixing u and d quarks.
    Physically: the energy PAID to bind different-flavor quarks.
  ★ (-0.0109265546) · σ_0  ← NEGATIVE (INPUT)
    Origin: combined from Hecke reduction remainder + d_ud
    The σ₀ coefficient absorbed contributions from:
      1. The original σ₀ term (from u_r–u_g crossing)
      2. The Hecke reduction of σ₀² (added +0.209060)
      3. The d coefficient of the u–d crossing (−0.104530)
    The small negative value means the d contribution
    slightly exceeded the Hecke energy release.
  ★ (+1.0000000000) · σ_1  ← POSITIVE (OUTPUT)
  ★ (+0.1045301610) · σ_0 · σ_1  ← POSITIVE (OUTPUT)
    This is the DOMINANT term — the hadron bound state.

  Type: quark–electron → positive crossing σ₀
  Element: σ₀  (c = 1, d = 0)

  Before: (-0.1045301610) · 𝟏

    (+0.1045301610) · σ_0 · σ_1 · σ_0

    Δ(σ_0 · σ_1 · σ_0): +0.000000 → +0.104530 (Δ = +0.104530)
    Δ(σ_1): +1.000000 → +0.000000 (Δ = -1.000000)
    Δ(σ_1 · σ_0): +0.000000 → +1.000000 (Δ = +1.000000)

  (-0.1068144700) · σ_0 · σ_1 · σ_2  [INPUT (consumed)]
  (+0.1045301610) · σ_1 · σ_0 · σ_2  [OUTPUT (produced)]
  (+1.0218531091) · σ_0 · σ_1 · σ_0 · σ_2  [OUTPUT (produced)]

  Net coefficient: +1.0086422455
  Markov trace (4-strand): 0.0605106743

PHYSICAL READING:
  The negative terms (-0.010 σ₁·σ₂ and -0.067 σ₀·σ₁·σ₂)
  are the Skein amplitude costs of binding quarks with
  different flavors (u–d). They entered through the d
  coefficient of the mixed crossing: d_ud = −½q·s.
  These are the 'raw materials' — the quark-pair mixing
  energy that was CONSUMED to build the hadron.

  The positive terms (+0.196 σ₁·σ₀·σ₂ and +1.286 σ₀·σ₁·σ₀·σ₂)
  are the BOUND STATE — the proton+electron that was PRODUCED.
  The dominant term σ₀·σ₁·σ₀·σ₂ encodes the full Borromean
  structure of the proton (σ₀·σ₁·σ₀) plus the electron Hopf
  link (σ₂).
